question: Um, what's the difference between a layover and a stopover? My trip goes through Singapore.
expected_answer: A layover is a connection where you wait for your next flight, usually less than 24 hours on an international trip, while a stopover is a deliberate break of more than 24 hours in the connecting city before you fly on.

key_facts: a layover is a connection of less than 24 hours on an international trip
a stopover is a planned stay of more than 24 hours

question: What's the difference in checked bags between Lite and Classic on my international flight?
expected_answer: On international flights Economy Lite includes 1 piece of checked baggage up to 23 kg, while Economy Classic includes 2 pieces up to 23 kg each.
answer_aliases: one piece versus two pieces of 23 kg

key_facts: Economy Lite fares include 1 piece of checked baggage up to 23 kg
Economy Classic and Economy Flex fares include 2 pieces of checked baggage up to 23 kg each

question: How many letters is an airport code? Is BNE on my tag just Brisbane?
expected_answer: Airport codes are three letters, assigned by IATA, so BNE is the three-letter code for Brisbane.

key_facts: IATA airport codes have three letters
BNE is Brisbane

question: How many bags can I check on a domestic Economy Classic fare?
expected_answer: On domestic flights Economy Classic includes 1 piece of checked baggage up to 23 kg.

key_facts: Economy Classic and Economy Flex fares include 1 piece of checked baggage up to 23 kg

question: How much is an extra checked bag on the Singapore flight if I pay online?
expected_answer: An extra bag up to 23 kg on an international flight is AUD 150 if bought online in Manage Booking up to 3 hours before departure, compared with AUD 220 at the airport.

key_facts: an additional checked bag up to 23 kg costs AUD 150 on international flights when bought online up to 3 hours before departure
AUD 220 on international flights

question: Can I keep my dive knife in my carry-on, or must it be checked?
expected_answer: No, knives aren't allowed in cabin baggage and security would confiscate it, so it needs to go in your checked bag.
answer_aliases: knives must go in checked baggage

key_facts: knives are prohibited in carry-on baggage
security will remove it; it should be packed in checked baggage

question: Can I bring my surfboard on the Cairns flight, or is that extra?
expected_answer: Yes; a board bag with up to 3 boards, up to 2.77 m long and 32 kg with fins removed, counts as part of your normal checked allowance and is only charged at the extra bag rate (AUD 75 online on domestic flights) if it takes you over that allowance.
answer_aliases: counts as part of your allowance

key_facts: Sports equipment is counted as part of your normal checked allowance
up to 3 boards may travel in one board bag, with a maximum length of 2.77 m and a maximum weight of 32 kg
AUD 75 on domestic flights

question: What does the 'NVA' next to my flight date on the e-ticket mean?
expected_answer: NVA stands for 'not valid after': that flight coupon can't be used after the date shown.

key_facts: NVA means not valid after
the coupon cannot be used after that date

question: Can I cancel for a full refund if I only booked this morning?
expected_answer: Only within 4 hours of purchase, and only if your first flight departs at least 7 days after you bought it; there is no 24-hour free cancellation period, so after 4 hours the normal fare rules apply.

key_facts: cancelled for a full refund only within 4 hours of purchase
only if the first flight departs at least 7 days after purchase
there is no 24-hour free cancellation period
meta.common_prior: Yes, within 24 hours of booking you can cancel for a full refund.

question: How much is it to change the date on an international Classic ticket?
expected_answer: Changing an Economy Classic international ticket costs AUD 250 per passenger plus any fare difference (and an AUD 25 service fee if done through the contact centre).

key_facts: date or flight changes cost AUD 250 on international flights per passenger, plus any fare difference

question: So why does it say on my ticket that it's operated by a different airline?
expected_answer: It's a codeshare: the flight is sold under one airline's flight number but flown by a partner airline's aircraft and crew, so you usually check in with the operating airline.

history.text: I'm booked on the Auckland flight on the fourth.
Yes, I've got it here, the morning departure.

key_facts: it is a codeshare flight
a partner airline operates the flight and crew

question: Can my sister take my ticket if I can't go? I'm on a Flex fare.
expected_answer: Yes, Economy Flex tickets can be transferred to a different person once, for AUD 150, at least 72 hours before the first flight; the person who made the booking requests it through the contact centre.

key_facts: allows a ticket to be transferred to a different person on Economy Flex and Business fares
A transfer costs AUD 150 per ticket, can be made only once per ticket
at least 72 hours before the first flight departs
meta.common_prior: No, airline tickets are non-transferable; only the named passenger can travel.

question: I'm flying Classic to LA, how long does jet lag usually take to wear off?
expected_answer: A common rule of thumb is about one day of recovery for each time zone (hour of time difference) you cross, and adjusting is often harder after flying east.
answer_aliases: about a day per time zone
a day per hour of time difference

key_facts: roughly one day per time zone crossed
body clock needs time to adjust to local time

question: How long's that good for? I'm hoping to use it later this year.
expected_answer: A travel credit is valid for 6 months from its issue date: you must make the new booking before then, though the flight itself can depart up to 12 months from the issue date.

history.text: I cancelled my Melbourne trip and you gave me a credit.
Yes, I can see the travel credit on your profile.

key_facts: travel credit is valid for 6 months from its issue date
must be used to make a new booking before it expires
departs within 12 months of the credit's issue date
meta.common_prior: 12 months from the date of issue.

question: So what's a bassinet seat exactly? Someone said I should ask for one for the baby.
expected_answer: A bassinet is a small cot that attaches to the wall in front of certain bulkhead seats so a baby can sleep during the flight; they have size and weight limits, need to be requested in advance, and the baby must be held on your lap for take-off, landing and turbulence.

key_facts: a bassinet is a cot fixed to the bulkhead in front of certain seats
the baby must be on a lap for take-off, landing and turbulence

question: Is it okay if he just sits on my lap the whole way?
expected_answer: No, on flights scheduled to take 9 hours or longer, including Brisbane to Vancouver, infants can't travel on a lap and need their own seat with an approved infant car seat, at 50% of the adult fare.
answer_aliases: no, he needs his own seat

history.text: We're flying Brisbane to Vancouver in March with our son.
Okay, and how old will he be by then?
Thanks, I've noted that on the booking.

key_facts: On flights scheduled to take 9 hours or longer, including Brisbane to Vancouver
must have their own seat with an approved infant car seat, at 50% of the adult fare
meta.common_prior: Yes, infants under 2 can travel on a parent's lap for about 10% of the adult fare.

question: How much is the Young Flyer service for my daughter on a domestic flight?
expected_answer: The Young Flyer service costs AUD 95 per child per flight on domestic flights, and it has to be booked through the contact centre at least 48 hours before departure.

key_facts: AUD 95 per child per flight on domestic flights
booked through the contact centre at least 48 hours before departure

question: My meal on the domestic flight tasted like nothing, why's food so bland up there?
expected_answer: Because the dry, low-pressure cabin air and engine noise reduce your sense of taste and smell, cutting how strongly you notice salt and sugar by roughly a third.

key_facts: dry, low-pressure cabin air reduces taste and smell
perception of salt and sweetness drops by roughly 30%

question: Why can't I just ask for a vegetarian meal when I check in?
expected_answer: Special meals must be requested at least 36 hours before departure, in Manage Booking or through the contact centre, because they're loaded by the caterers in advance; they can't be ordered at check-in.

key_facts: Special meals must be requested at least 36 hours before departure
a special meal cannot be ordered at check-in

question: If the board says 'late inbound aircraft', is my flight about to get cancelled?
expected_answer: Not necessarily: it means the plane scheduled to operate your flight is arriving late from its previous flight, so your departure is delayed until it lands and is turned around, rather than cancelled.

key_facts: the aircraft for your flight is arriving late from its previous trip
your flight waits for it to arrive and be prepared

question: If you cancel my flight, can I just get my money back instead?
expected_answer: Yes, you can choose a full refund to your original payment method, but you must request it within 28 days of the cancellation through Manage Booking or the contact centre, otherwise the booking is automatically converted into a travel credit.

key_facts: receive a full refund to the original payment method
A refund request must be made within 28 days of the cancellation
if no choice is made within 28 days, the booking is automatically converted into a travel credit
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, if the airline cancels your flight you're entitled to a full refund and it will be paid back automatically.

question: What does 'minimum connection time' mean? You guys mentioned it when I was booking.
expected_answer: It's the shortest gap between an arriving and a departing flight that the airport and airline consider enough for you and your bags to make the transfer; connections shorter than that aren't sold on one booking.
answer_aliases: minimum time to transfer between flights

key_facts: the shortest time allowed between connecting flights at an airport
shorter connections are not sold as one itinerary

question: How much time do I need between landing from Bali and a domestic flight in Brisbane?
expected_answer: The minimum connection time at Brisbane from an international to a domestic flight is 90 minutes, since you collect your bags and clear customs and biosecurity before re-checking them.

key_facts: international to domestic 90 minutes
collect your bags and clear customs and biosecurity before re-checking them

question: What happens if I miss my second flight because the first was late? I booked them separately.
expected_answer: If both separate bookings are on Coralwind Airways and you left at least 3 hours between them, you'll be rebooked free on the next available flight; with less than 3 hours standard change fees apply, and partner-airline connections on separate bookings are never protected.

key_facts: if both separate bookings are on Coralwind Airways flights and you left at least 3 hours
we will rebook you free of charge on the next available flight
With less than 3 hours between them, standard change fees apply
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: On separate bookings the airline isn't responsible, so you'd have to buy a new ticket for the missed flight.

question: Another airline's offering to give me a status match, how's that work exactly?
expected_answer: A status match is when an airline gives you an equivalent tier in its own frequent flyer programme based on proof of the status you already hold with another airline, often on a trial basis.

key_facts: an airline grants an equivalent tier based on status held with another airline

question: How many status credits do I need to get to Gold?
expected_answer: Gold needs 600 status credits earned in a membership year.

key_facts: Gold at 600 status credits
earned in a membership year

question: Why does my points balance keep dropping when I fly with you all the time?
expected_answer: Points expire 36 months after the end of the month in which they were earned, and flying or earning more doesn't extend existing points, so the oldest points expire first even if you're active.

key_facts: points expire 36 months after the end of the month in which they were earned
Flying or earning more does not extend existing points
the oldest points always expire first
meta.common_prior: Points don't expire as long as there's some account activity (e.g. every 18 months), so a regular flyer shouldn't lose any.

question: Why do I have to put it upright for landing then?
expected_answer: Seats must be upright for take-off and landing so the row behind has a clear path to evacuate and the seat is locked in the position it's certified to protect you in during an emergency.

history.text: I'm in Business to Tokyo next week, the lie-flat seats.
Yes, that aircraft has them in every Business row.

key_facts: upright seats keep exit paths clear for an evacuation
the seat is locked in its crash-tested position

question: How much is a lounge day pass in Brisbane before my Sydney flight?
expected_answer: A lounge day pass costs AUD 65 at the domestic lounges (AUD 90 at the Brisbane international lounge), sold in the app up to 1 hour before departure.

key_facts: lounge day pass for AUD 65 at domestic lounges
AUD 90 at the Brisbane international lounge

question: Um, can I use my points to upgrade to Business on the Tokyo flight?
expected_answer: Yes, but only from an Economy Classic or Economy Flex fare, not Lite, and the request must be made at least 72 hours before departure; Brisbane to Tokyo costs 30,000 points from Flex or 40,000 from Classic.

key_facts: only on Economy Classic and Economy Flex fares; Economy Lite fares cannot be upgraded with points
Upgrade requests must be made at least 72 hours before departure
costs 30,000 points one way from Economy Flex and 40,000 points from Economy Classic
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you can use points to upgrade to Business any time, even at the airport, subject to seat availability.
